docRequirement: plugins/org.md#recommend-plugins (was line 158 of the retired discover-plugins page) binds the Discover surface: "When your administrator has allowlisted the marketplace via the [`pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) managed setting, plugins marked as relevant to your current working directory are pinned at the top with a **suggested for this directory** label." Three obligations follow, spelled out by the two pages this one links: (1) a marketplace entry may carry a `relevance` object with `topic` and `signals` (plugins/marketplace-reference.md#entry-and-plugin-json (was line 221 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page), plugin-relevance.md field reference), of which `cwd` is the signal this sentence names; (2) `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces` is a managed-settings-only array of marketplace NAMES, and "No marketplace-declared suggestions surface without this allowlist", with a name only taking effect when "its registered source is also declared in managed settings, either as the `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry for that name or as an entry of `strictKnownMarketplaces`" (settings.md:302); (3) a matching plugin is pinned above the other Discover results with an annotation naming the matching signal, e.g. `suggested for this directory` (plugin-relevance.md, § How it works).
current: Nothing on that path exists. (a) `relevance` is dropped at catalog parse: `MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS` is an explicit allowlist of entry keys (packages/shared/src/marketplace/external-catalog-adapters.ts:153-166 — comment: "Deliberately an ALLOWLIST, not a copy of the entry") and the copy loop in `parseMarketplaceEntryDefinition` (same file:234-255) writes only allowlisted keys into `fields`, so `relevance` never reaches `ExternalPluginCatalogProposal` (:83-100) nor `MarketplaceCatalogItem` (packages/shared/src/marketplace/types.ts:340-400). The drop is pinned by a test whose fixture declares `relevance: { keywords: ['review'] }` under the comment "Not a field any adapter reads — must not travel with the definition" and asserts the carried key set is exactly `['description','mcpServers','skills','version']` (packages/shared/src/marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:407-433). (b) `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces` has zero source readers repo-wide: it is absent from `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and from `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534), and `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727-733) therefore strips it with `invalid managed Pi policy key: pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`. The two sibling managed marketplace keys ARE implemented — `strictKnownMarketplaces` (parsed :1428-1433, carried packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts:177/:304/:388-393) and `extraKnownMarketplaces` (parsed :1434-1439, delivered registry-source.ts:348-381), wired from packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:303-310. (c) No suggestion surface exists to pin into: the browse list is `MarketplaceService.list` merging Skills Market rows with registry rows in catalog order (packages/shared/src/marketplace/service.ts:97-113, mergeRegistryItems :202-221), projected path-free by `toSafeMarketplaceCatalogItem` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts:576-615) into `SafeMarketplaceCatalogItem` (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:467-499, which has no suggestion/pin field), and rendered in load order after `filterItemsForMarketplace` (apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/plugin-marketplace-filter.ts:84-90, called at apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/PluginsPage.tsx:246) and `capListForRender` (:119-136). `grep -rna "suggested for\|suggestedFor\|spinnerTips"` over packages/ and apps/ returns one unrelated Codex schema string; the only `relevance` hits in source are a quoted doc sentence (packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:832), the test fixture above, and the fuzzy-search scorer (packages/shared/src/search/fuzzy.ts) — a sibling-subsystem homonym, not this feature. (d) The `cwd` fact the matcher would need is reachable server-side but unused on this path: the LIST handler ignores its context (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/marketplace.ts:148-155, `_ctx`), while the same file already resolves a session cwd via `deps.sessionManager.getWorkingDirectory(sessionId, workspaceId)` at :541-543.
divergence: Not a wrong key name or a narrower value — the whole three-part mechanism is absent: the entry field is deliberately dropped, the managed key is not in the schema (and is actively rejected as unknown), and there is no Discover-tab pin or annotation to receive a match. One further gap is structural rather than merely missing code: settings.md:302 allowlists by marketplace NAME, and Nessy persists no marketplace name. `PluginMarketplaceRegistry` (packages/shared/src/plugins/store.ts:42-62) stores `id`, `source`, `refName`, `displayName`; the catalog's own `name` (`ExternalPluginCatalogDto.name`, external-catalog-adapters.ts:55) is parsed and never stored. A delivered marketplace is the only case with a real name today, because `deliverMarketplaces` passes `displayName: entry.name` from the managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` key (registry-source.ts:358-362); a user-added registry's `displayName` is derived from its source string (`registryDisplayName` :952-954). The doc's own source-correspondence rule happens to cover the delivered case exactly, so the name identity gap only bites for a marketplace allowlisted by name whose source is declared through `strictKnownMarketplaces` instead.

change.what: Parse `relevance` into a NEW typed optional `relevance?: PluginMarketplaceRelevanceV1` on the proposal (:83-100). Do NOT add the key to `MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS` (:153-166): that allowlist feeds `entryDefinition.fields`, which is persisted with the install record on `PluginOrigin.marketplaceEntry` (packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:54-61), and relevance is browse-time matching data, not a plugin-defining field — keeping it off that allowlist preserves the allowlist's stated invariant. New validator enforces the documented caps: `topic` string <= 64 chars; `signals.cwd` <= 10 patterns of <= 256 chars; `signals.cli` <= 10 of <= 64; `signals.hosts` <= 20 of <= 128 rejecting any entry with a scheme, port or path; `signals.filesRead` <= 10 of <= 256; `signals.manifestDeps` <= 10 objects of `{file, pattern}` RegExp sources <= 256. Unknown keys under `relevance` and `relevance.signals` are ignored, not errors (plugin-relevance.md Note); a `relevance` that is not an object gets a warning diagnostic and is dropped, with at least one signal required for the block to be usable.

Add `relevance?: PluginMarketplaceRelevanceV1` (additive, omit-when-empty) beside `marketplaceEntry` at :390-395. Note this rides the on-disk parsed-catalog cache (`PersistedCatalogEntry.items`, registry-source.ts:124-131), so an existing cache entry simply lacks the field until its signature changes and it re-fetches — additive-safe, no schemaVersion bump required.
Carry `proposal.relevance` onto the produced `MarketplaceCatalogItem` (:214, :241), omit-when-absent, exactly as `entryVersion`/`entryDescription` are carried today.

Four edits. (1) Add `readonly pluginSuggestionMarketplaces?: readonly string[]` beside the two marketplace keys (:141/:158), documented from settings.md:302. (2) Parse it next to the other two (:1428-1439) as a plain grant list of marketplace names validated by the existing `MARKETPLACE_NAME` regex (managed-marketplace-entries.ts:262) with the same 128-entry cap; absent and `[]` mean the same thing here (no suggestions), so it does NOT need the absent-vs-empty distinction `strictKnownMarketplaces` needs, and a wholly invalid value must empty rather than widen. (3) Add `'pluginSuggestionMarketplaces'` to `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (:501-534) and to the emitted frozen object (:1440-1450). (4) Add it to `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_WIDENING_KEYS` (:555-563): its presence hands a surface OUT, so leaving it to the default "constraining" classification would let `isManagedPolicyTightening` adopt a widening mid-turn.
Pass `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces` through alongside the existing two spreads at :303-310, same omit-when-undefined shape.

Accept `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces?: readonly string[]` in the options interface (:147-192) and in the factory options (:1079-1095), store it on the class (:296-307), and expose a predicate `isSuggestionAllowed(registry)` implementing settings.md:302's TWO-part gate: the registry's marketplace name is in the allowlist AND the registry's registered source is itself declared in managed settings — i.e. it was delivered under that name via `extraKnownMarketplaces` (the `displayName: entry.name` add at :358-362) or its source matches `strictKnownMarketplaces` via the existing `isManagedMarketplaceAllowed`/`managedMarketplaceSourceIdentity` pair (:388-393). Drop the official-Anthropic-name exemption: Nessy registers no official marketplace, so implementing the exemption would be an unreachable branch.

Add `catalogName?: string` — the catalog manifest's own declared `name` — and stamp it when a catalog resolves, so a marketplace has a NAME to match the allowlist against. Without it only delivered registries (whose `displayName` IS the managed key's name) can be matched. `marketplaces.json` is schema-versioned (`PluginMarketplaceRegistryFile`, :64-68); an added optional field is additive, no migration.

New file. Implement the `cwd` signal exactly as plugin-relevance.md specifies: glob patterns matched against the session working directory as an ABSOLUTE path and, when inside a git repository, also as a path relative to the repository root; forward-slash normalized; case-insensitive; every pattern matches the directory itself and everything under it, so `infra`, `infra/` and `infra/**` behave identically. Return the matched signal so the annotation can name it (`suggested for this directory`). Scope this change to `cwd` only — `cli`, `hosts`, `filesRead` and `manifestDeps` need per-session history Nessy does not record and are what plugin-relevance.md, not this page, binds.

Add an additive, omit-when-empty display-only field — e.g. `suggestion?: { signal: 'cwd' }` — to the Safe row (:467-499). Carry the SIGNAL, not a rendered sentence, so the label stays translatable in the renderer. This is a wire boundary: nothing path-bearing may cross, and the field must stay optional so an older renderer is unaffected.

The LIST handler at :148-155 currently ignores `_ctx`; make it read `ctx.workspaceId` and resolve the session cwd through `deps.sessionManager.getWorkingDirectory(...)` (the pattern already present at :541-543), evaluate `matchCwdSignal` only for rows whose registry passes `isSuggestionAllowed`, and pass the result into `toSafeMarketplaceCatalogItem` (:576-615) as the new `suggestion` field. No allowlist entry, no cwd, or no `relevance` -> field absent and the list is byte-identical to today.

Stable-partition rows carrying `suggestion` to the front after `filterItemsForMarketplace` (plugin-marketplace-filter.ts:84-90) and BEFORE `capListForRender` (:119-136), so a pinned row can never fall outside the render window; render a `suggested for this directory` badge on the pinned card. Keep the partition stable so unpinned order is untouched.

One key for the badge under an existing prefix (e.g. `sourcesList.*`/`skillsList.*` sibling for the plugins browse). Add to BOTH locale files, alphabetically sorted; `bun run lint:i18n:parity` and `lint:i18n:sorted` gate it.

blastRadius: Crosses BOTH a wire boundary and a persistence boundary, so it is a risk trigger by this repo's rule. Wire: `SafeMarketplaceCatalogItem` (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:467-499) is the renderer-facing Safe projection — consumed by apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useMarketplaceItems.ts (24 call sites through `SafeMarketplaceCatalogItem`, plus `marketplaceBrowseRows`/`collapseDuplicateCatalogRows` at :306-361) and by apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/plugin-install-state.ts; existing renderer tests are apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/__tests__/{useMarketplaceItems,marketplace-duplicate-rows}.test.ts and pages/__tests__/plugins-page-install-state.test.ts. Persistence: `MarketplaceCatalogItem` is stored verbatim in the on-disk parsed-catalog cache (`PersistedCatalogEntry`, registry-source.ts:124-131) and the same rows feed `findCatalogItem` (:471-490) which install routes through — an added optional field is additive, but anything mandatory would strand every cached catalog. Managed policy: `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` is stated over by three separate whole-key-set invariants — the tightening predicate (`isManagedPolicyTightening`, whose widening set decides mid-turn vs turn-boundary adoption), the delivered-vs-file composition (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts), and the delivered-policy reachability test — and the enforced policy round-trips through a 0600 delivered cache file. `refuseUnknownKeys` also means an admin's existing file changes behaviour the moment the key is accepted: what is stripped with a warning today starts being enforced. Reader of the drop: packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:446-450. Imported-plugin path: any Claude marketplace catalog carrying `relevance` (the field is live upstream since Claude Code v2.1.152) currently parses fine and will keep parsing fine — the parse must stay tolerant of unknown sub-keys or a newer upstream marketplace starts erroring.
userImpact: One half is observable today, the other is not. Observable, admin-facing: an administrator who copies Claude's documented `managed-settings.json` example (plugin-relevance.md § Enable suggestions) into Nessy's managed policy has the key REJECTED — `refuseUnknownKeys` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:727-733) strips it with `invalid managed Pi policy key: pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`, and the config doctor prints it under "Invalid managed entries (N)" (packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:446-450). Their sibling keys in the same file (`extraKnownMarketplaces`, `strictKnownMarketplaces`) are honoured, so the file half-applies and reports a defect the admin cannot fix. End-user half: none observable — a plugin whose marketplace entry declares `relevance` renders in the plugins browse list in ordinary catalog order with no badge, indistinguishable from a plugin that declares nothing, and no suggestion appears anywhere. It would surface the moment an org publishes a `relevance`-bearing internal marketplace and expects the directory-matched plugin to be pinned for its engineers.
notes: Every file cited was read in this session (via codegraph verbatim source or Read); the doc pages were fetched with `curl -sL` (discover-plugins.md, settings.md, plugin-marketplaces.md, plugin-relevance.md) rather than WebFetch. Scope decision worth reviewing: the spec deliberately covers only the `cwd` signal and the Discover-tab pin, because that is what plugins/org.md#recommend-plugins (was line 158 of the retired discover-plugins page) binds. plugin-relevance.md additionally specifies a spinner tip and a session-start notification, plus four history-based signals (`cli`, `hosts`, `filesRead`, `manifestDeps`) — Nessy has no spinner-tip system at all (`grep -rna 'spinnerTips'` over packages/ and apps/ is empty) and records no per-session shell-command or files-read history for the other signals, so those are separate, larger work and arguably a separate finding against plugin-relevance.md, which the phase-2 sweep did not file. Two things I could not settle from code alone and that need an owner decision at implementation time: (1) whether to persist the catalog's declared `name` on the registry row (needed for the `strictKnownMarketplaces`-declared case) or to accept matching only delivered marketplaces by their `extraKnownMarketplaces` key, which is strictly narrower than the doc but covers the corporate deployment this fork actually has; (2) whether the Discover pin should be per-visit one-shot as plugin-relevance.md describes ("The Discover tab pins a given plugin once; later visits list it in normal order") — that needs a per-plugin shown-once record with no obvious existing home in this repo, and the sweep's quoted sentence does not require it.
